scope: Three review findings, each reproduced before the fix and checked against retained acceptance data after it.

findings.title: the private Mesa build tree breaks the standard build and test entry point
findings.reproduced: plain "colcon test" exits with: Duplicate package names not supported: MesonTemp: local_data/mesa-source-build/build/meson-private/cmake_directx-headers and .../cmake_lua. colcon list also picks up CompInfo and data, four spurious packages in all.
findings.also_found: with --packages-select it does not fail, so only a full-workspace run hits it, which is the run made before a release
findings.fix: write COLCON_IGNORE into the build root immediately after creating it, before anything else is written
findings.note: local_data is gitignored, so the marker in the existing tree cannot be committed; the durable half has to live in the script
findings.verified: colcon list finds no package under local_data; full colcon test runs again, 7 packages, 362 tests at that point

findings.title: a legally discarded short tail made the whole session unprocessable offline
findings.reproduced: accept_tier_0500 holds 670 blocks spanning ids 0 to 678 with nine gaps, the first 66 to 68, while accept_rated_6 with no discards is contiguous. The old check required block_id == index.
findings.mechanism: gz_linescan.cpp:642 logs tail_discarded to the raw capture events.jsonl and the discard consumes a block id via block_++
findings.fix: read the sensor's own event log, allow exactly the ids it recorded as discarded, and keep rejecting every other gap. The evidence is checked rather than trusted: an event must declare 0 < rows < minimum_rows, ids may not repeat, and an id claimed discarded may not also have a file.
findings.verified: the new parser run against the real event log of the 0.5 m/s run resolves ten discarded ids (rows 712 to 806 against a 1000 row minimum); the nine numbering gaps are all accounted for and the tenth, 679, lies past the last block so it forms no gap. Four new tests, three of them rejections.

findings.title: the coverage audit missed holes in the middle of the execution trace
findings.reproduced: cutting the trace to its first and last record still returned ESTIMATED_COMPLETE with no issue raised
findings.risk: quality_windows is derived from the same records, so a steering reconfiguration inside a hole is invisible and the block is certified anyway
findings.fix: compare each interval against the control step the following record declares for itself. A slow tick still leaves evidence and its gap equals what it declares; a longer gap means records are absent.
findings.why_not_a_fixed_threshold: across 193,730 record pairs in six acceptance runs the interval and the declared step agree exactly, deviation 0. accept_rated_5 contains one 0.352 s step whose record declares 0.352 s, so any fixed threshold below that would have rejected sound data and any threshold above it would still miss smaller holes.
findings.correction_to_review: the review stated the retained acceptance logs have a maximum interval of about 22 ms. That holds for accept_rated_6 and accept_tier_0500 but not accept_rated_5, whose largest interval is 0.352 s. It sits at t=9.45 to 9.81, before the mission began, with capture inactive and no block spanning it. The quantity that matters is the largest interval inside a capture block: 0.0230, 0.0210 and 0.0220 s for the three counted runs.
findings.verified: the new check reports zero gaps in all six acceptance runs, so no closed result is retroactively invalidated

tests.detail: four for the tail-discard path in agv_linescan, two for the trace-gap path in agv_mission, one of which guards against false positives on a slow control step

fixture_correction: the coverage test fixture emitted execution records without control_dt_s, which the real sensor never omits (present in 193,730 of 193,730 records). The fixture was made realistic rather than the check weakened to tolerate its absence.
